name: Henry A Plain Jr
current_role: Partner, Morgenthaler Ventures (life sciences) and Founding Partner / managing director of LSV Associates II (Lightstone Ventures)
profile: Hank Plain is a medtech venture investor. After 12 years at Eli Lilly (from 1980) he was CEO of Perclose (IPO, later acquired by Abbott), co-founded eight device companies with The Foundry incubator, and joined Morgenthaler in 2007; he co-founded Lightstone Ventures, whose LSV II funds hold a >10% stake in Shoulder Innovations (NYSE: SI, IPO 2025).
interesting_fact: He led investments in Ardian, the renal-denervation company incubated at The Foundry that Medtronic acquired in 2011; his former boards also include Acclarent, Claret Medical and Twelve, all later acquired.
deep_cut_fact: Outside venture capital he chairs the Naval Postgraduate School Foundation in Monterey, CA, sits on the board of The First Tee of Monterey County, and holds a B.S. in Finance from the University of Missouri-Columbia.
notes: SEC listing is via LSV Associates II (Lightstone), which holds the Shoulder Innovations stake; he is not on the SI board (colleague Mike Carusi is), per the 2025 424B4. Pure medtech VC with no energy angle. Best route is the Morgenthaler/Lightstone office.

name: Michael H. Train
current_role: Senior Vice President and Chief Sustainability Officer, Emerson (NYSE: EMR)
profile: Mike Train is a 35-year Emerson veteran. He joined in 1991 as an international planner, ran Process Management Asia-Pacific, the Rosemount business and global sales, then was president of Emerson from 2018 to 2021. In March 2021 he became Emerson's first Chief Sustainability Officer, steering its decarbonization and energy-transition automation strategy.
interesting_fact: Before becoming its first CSO he was President of Emerson (2018-2021), overseeing software and digital technology, major investments, international growth and global shared services.
deep_cut_fact: He is an electrical engineer from the General Motors Institute (now Kettering University), a 2008 Eisenhower Fellow, and chairs the board of trustees of Ranken Technical College in St. Louis. Early on he led Emerson's operations in Japan and Korea.

public_contacts.value: Joele Frank, Wilkinson Brimmer Katcher (Emerson media contact), (212) 355-4449

notes: Strong energy-transition and industrial-automation angle for the podcast. Corporate executive, not a founder; outreach should go through Emerson communications.

name: John Wesley Hardin
current_role: President - Electronic Instruments, AMETEK Inc. (NYSE: AME); executive officer since 2008
profile: Wes Hardin is a long-serving AMETEK operating executive. He joined in December 1998 as sales and marketing director of the Dixson dashboard-instruments division, became its VP/GM in 2001, moved to SVP Aerospace & Defense, and since July 2008 has been one of the presidents of AMETEK's Electronic Instruments Group.
interesting_fact: He came up through AMETEK Dixson, which makes custom dashboard instruments and displays for heavy trucks, construction and farm equipment. AMETEK's CEO credited his leadership of Dixson's INTERLINK Next Generation Instrument line.
deep_cut_fact: Before AMETEK he was a Senior Project Engineer at McDonnell Douglas and later Director of Engineering at Furon Company. He holds an EE degree from the University of Missouri-Columbia and a marketing MBA from Webster University. Colleagues know him as 'Wes'.

public_contacts.value: kevin.coleman@ametek.com (Kevin Coleman, VP Investor Relations & Treasurer, 610.889.5247)

notes: Low-profile corporate operator with almost no personal public presence. AMETEK lists several 'President - Electronic Instruments' officers, and his 2026 status comes from aggregators (no retirement announcement found). Go through AMETEK corporate communications/IR.

name: Paul A Jacobson
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, General Motors (since Dec 2020)
profile: Paul Jacobson has been GM's CFO since December 2020. Before that he spent his whole career at Delta Air Lines, joining as a financial analyst in 1997 and serving as CFO from 2012. At GM he manages capital allocation through tariffs and the 2026 EV restructuring, guiding to stronger cash flow in 2027.
interesting_fact: He joined GM from outside the auto industry. He had spent 23 years at Delta and became its CFO at about 40, after starting as a financial analyst straight out of business school.
deep_cut_fact: He decided to be a pilot at age seven after his first flight, but was medically disqualified from Air Force ROTC pilot training at Auburn because of childhood asthma. He studied aviation management instead (Auburn '94) and told his Vanderbilt MBA placement director he wanted a job 'with an airline, preferably Delta.'
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; the SEC insider listing comes from his GM stock compensation. Reach him through GM corporate communications/IR. Relevant for EV/energy and capital-allocation topics.

name: Michele Buck
current_role: Special Advisor to The Hershey Company (retired as Chairman, President & CEO in Aug 2025); Director, JPMorgan Chase (since 2025)
profile: Michele Buck spent 17 years at Kraft/Nabisco and Frito-Lay, then joined Hershey in 2005. She became its first female CEO in 2017 and chair in 2019, and turned it into a 'snacking powerhouse' with deals such as the $1.6B Amplify (SkinnyPop) purchase. Kirk Tanner succeeded her as CEO in August 2025; she now advises Hershey and sits on JPMorgan Chase's board.
interesting_fact: She was Hershey's first female CEO, and her $1.6B purchase of Amplify Snack Brands in 2017 was at the time the largest acquisition in Hershey's history.
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in Carlisle, PA, about 45 minutes from Hershey, and toured the chocolate factory as a child. She started a paper route at 10, later sold Avon door to door, and her first job after Shippensburg University was fiscal analyst at the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue.
notes: The input lists her as Hershey Chairman/CEO, which is outdated: she retired in Aug 2025 (per her JPMorgan bio) and is now a Special Advisor. Still a JPM director. Best routes are Hershey corporate communications or the JPMorgan corporate secretary.
